sections.content:
Interesting! Clicking (21,19) — the center of the blue 4x4 — changed only one cell: (63,0) from W to G. Row 63 is the white strip at the bottom (the HUD row). So clicking the blue block did nothing to the gameplay board, but the white bar at the bottom changed: previously row 63 was all W, now it's G followed by 63 Ws. So the bottom white bar is a timer/progress bar that shrinks with each action! It lost one pixel at the left end (col 0 became G).
So the bottom bar is a timer/step bar. Each action consumes 1 pixel. It started at 64 Ws (row 63). Now it's 63.
And clicking the blue block did nothing else. So MOUSE on the blue block = no selection. Maybe MOUSE is used to click on the right-side target? Or maybe the click needs to be on a specific interactive object. Or maybe the arrow keys move the "selected" piece, and the mouse selects a piece — but the click on the blue block didn't show any selection change.
Hmm, wait, maybe the click did select the piece but there's no visual indicator. Let me try the arrow keys and see if the blue block moves.
Actually, let me think about the timer: 6638 seconds remaining, and the bar is 64 px. The bar probably decreases by 1 per action. So we have about 64 actions?? Wait, the bar is 64 Ws and lost 1 per action. Hmm, but time_remaining is 6638 seconds. The bar might represent remaining steps (64). So we need to solve within 64 actions. This is a constraint: be efficient!
Wait, actually let me double-check: at step 1 (before the action), row 63 was all W (64 Ws). After 1 action, 63 Ws. So yes, 1 px per action. So the budget is about 63 actions remaining.
Now, about the game mechanics. Let me try arrow keys. If nothing is selected, the arrows might move the cursor... but I don't see a cursor. Let me try RIGHT and see what changes.
Actually, wait. Let me reconsider: maybe the mouse click selects a piece, and then the arrow keys move it. The click on (21,19) was on the blue block. If the selection has no visual change, then pressing RIGHT should move the blue block 1 to the right (if there's no collision). Let me test: press RIGHT, take a diff.
If the blue block moves, great. If not, try other interpretations:
- Maybe the arrows move a hidden cursor, and the mouse places something.
- Maybe you need to click twice (pick up, then place).
- Maybe the mouse click on the right-side frame is what matters.
Let me try RIGHT now and take a diff.
